outcome: Give semantic expressions two text-cleaning functions (GAPS G5): replace(text, from, to) and regexp_replace(text, pattern, replacement), each replacing every occurrence, so values read as text with markup, units or separators can be cleaned and cast without a raw_query.
criteria: Expressions accept replace(text, from, to) and regexp_replace(text, pattern, replacement), both over strings and returning a string, each replacing every occurrence or match; README.md and the transform tool description list them, saying they clean values read as text while rendering an answer stays with export (MADR 0005).

In a derive, try_cast(regexp_replace(x, '[^0-9.]', '') as bigint) turns '**18,713,981** 股' into 18713981, and replace(x, ',', '') removes every comma of '1,234,567' (tested on data unrelated to any benchmark).

regexp_replace written with a fourth options argument made of the letters g, i and c resolves to the three-argument form with a resolution note (g is implied; i prefixes a literal pattern with (?i)); any other fourth argument is refused with the signature.
A pattern the regular-expression engine rejects fails the transform with a structured error response rather than an unhandled exception, and the full test suite passes.

dispositions.note: replace(string, string, string) and regexp_replace(string, string, string) are in the function allowlist, compiled to DuckDB replace and to regexp_replace with 'g'; README's allowlist and the transform tool description list them as cleaning a value read as text before a cast, with rendering left to export (MADR 0005).

try_cast(regexp_replace(shares, '[^0-9.]', '') as bigint) gives 18713981 and 1234567 as integers; replace(shares, ',', '') removes every comma; regexp_replace(note, '-', '+') replaces every dash where DuckDB alone replaces the first. Data: two invented holdings.

'gi' resolves to three arguments with the pattern '(?i)rated' and the note 'every match is replaced without options; (?i) makes the pattern case-insensitive'; 'm' is refused as INVALID_TRANSFORM with the signature regexp_replace(string, string, string).
the pattern '(' fails with an EXECUTION_FAILED response ('missing )'); 409 passed, 8 skipped.

note: The options argument is folded in the resolver, as strftime's reversed arguments are, so the canonical IR keeps one form. Patterns are checked by the engine at execution, not at resolution: the engine's RE2 syntax is not Python's, so a Python pre-check would both miss and invent errors.
